title: Just a Game Engine
author: Sure_Excuse_8824
selftext:
In addition to writing books, I also develop software. Over the past several months I have been working on something I am pretty excited about called Just a Game Engine (JGE). The idea is this - Many writers, comic artists, D&D and tabletop game masters, and other creatives would love the chance to see their worlds as a video game. But there are two major problems.

**1.** Working with the traditional game dev engines requires a high level of programing expertise. It takes years to learn. Time better spent on the skills they have already worked for years mastering - storytelling and world building.

**2.** Prompt to Code tools are a joke. They give you a quick demo that the *machine*s that *shall not be named* decides is the game. It is not anything that resembles your original world. Not your creative ideas.

So I decided to create an engine that allows us to build games using the skills we already have - language. Everything you build is yours. Your world. Your rules. Born from your HUMAN creativity. The engine has 0 creative input.

If what you build is a bad game, that's on you.

And it's not a shortcut either. It takes about as much time, and certainly as much work, as engineers spend building on engines like Unity or UnReal. The difference is you are using your narrative skills as the programming language. So this isn't some flashy toy that is meant to give users constant dopamine hits and ends up producing  
yet another in a long line of crappy demos that go nowhere.

I'm in the final stages before beta testing. But I hope to have it ready for release in about a year.  
So be on the lookout.
